therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: thromboxane A2 synthesis inhibition / platelet function modulation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: healthy volunteers studied in crossover design to assess acetaminophen's effect on platelet thromboxane production and interaction with aspirin
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Percent change in serum thromboxane B2

results.effect_size: Acetaminophen 1000 mg/d alone: -6.5% inhibition; Acetaminophen 4000 mg/d: 21.9% inhibition; Ibuprofen 800 mg/d: 62.6% inhibition; Aspirin combinations: ~97% inhibition
results.target_engagement_evidence: Aspirin-containing arms showed ~97% inhibition of serum thromboxane B2, confirming COX-1 inhibition by aspirin; acetaminophen alone showed minimal inhibition (-6.5% at 1000 mg/d, 21.9% at 4000 mg/d)
biomarker_changes: Serum thromboxane B2 inhibition: Phase 1a aspirin+acetaminophen arms ~97%
Serum thromboxane B2 inhibition: Phase 1b acetaminophen 1000 mg/d alone: -6.5% (no meaningful inhibition)
Serum thromboxane B2 inhibition: Phase 2 acetaminophen 4000 mg/d: 21.9%
Serum thromboxane B2 inhibition: Phase 2 ibuprofen 800 mg/d: 62.6%
Arachidonic acid-induced platelet aggregation inhibition: Phase 1a aspirin+acetaminophen arms ~90-95%

dose_info.dose: acetaminophen 1000 mg or 4000 mg/d; aspirin 81 mg; ibuprofen 800 mg/d
dose_info.schedule: acetaminophen 1000 mg once daily x6 days (Phase 1b); acetaminophen 1000 mg q6h x3 days (Phase 2); ibuprofen 200 mg q6h x3 days (Phase 2); aspirin 81 mg single dose (Phase 1a)

context.indication: Myocardial Infarction, Arthritis (mechanistic study of acetaminophen effects on platelet thromboxane and aspirin interaction)
context.investigator_commentary: Crossover mechanistic study examining whether acetaminophen inhibits thromboxane B2 and platelet aggregation, and whether it interferes with aspirin's antiplatelet effect. Acetaminophen alone showed minimal thromboxane inhibition; aspirin-containing arms showed ~97% inhibition regardless of acetaminophen co-administration or dosing order. ANOVA p>0.05 for primary endpoint comparisons.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Acetaminophen co-administration (before or after aspirin) was hypothesized to interfere with aspirin's irreversible COX-1 inhibition and thereby reduce aspirin's antiplatelet effect on thromboxane synthesis
modulation_entries.citation: Phase 1a aspirin+acetaminophen arms showed ~97% inhibition of serum thromboxane B2 regardless of dosing order (Aspirin First or Aspirin Last), with ANOVA p>0.05, indicating acetaminophen did not meaningfully modulate aspirin's antiplatelet biology
